body.text: Same-origin JSON API at /api/items. An item is {id: integer, name: string, quantity: integer, unit: string or null, expires: YYYY-MM-DD or null, created_at: string}. Name is trimmed and must contain 1–80 characters; quantity is a nonnegative integer, not a boolean; unit is optional text or null; expires is a real calendar date or null. POST /api/items accepts name, quantity, and optional unit and expires; returns 201 and the created item. GET /api/items returns 200 and an array sorted by expiry ascending, nulls last, with id as a stable tie-breaker. Optional q performs case-insensitive substring name search; optional expiring_within is a nonnegative integer and includes dated items through today plus DAYS, including expired items. Both filters combine. PATCH /api/items/{id} accepts a nonempty subset of name, quantity, unit, and expires and returns 200 and the updated item. POST /api/items/{id}/consume accepts {"amount": positive integer}, atomically subtracts it, and returns 200 and the updated item; insufficient quantity returns 409. DELETE /api/items/{id} returns 204 with no body. Invalid input returns 400 JSON {"error":"..."}; an unknown item returns 404 JSON {"error":"..."}; conflict returns 409 JSON {"error":"..."}. Today means the server's local calendar date. The UI's seven-day section includes today through today plus seven days and separately marks earlier dates as expired.

scopeIn: Build ShelfLife, a small local pantry tracker for one household. Use Python 3.12 standard library only (sqlite3, http.server, csv, json); no third-party packages, no network access at runtime, no build step.
Backend: `python server.py --port PORT --db PATH` serves a JSON API and the web UI on 127.0.0.1.
Items have: id, name (1-80 chars), quantity (integer >= 0), unit (text, optional), expires (YYYY-MM-DD or null), created_at.
GET /api/items (optional ?expiring_within=DAYS, ?q=TEXT name search) returns items sorted by expiry (nulls last).

POST /api/items creates; PATCH /api/items/{id} updates quantity/name/unit/expires; POST /api/items/{id}/consume {"amount": n} reduces quantity (never below 0; 409 if amount exceeds quantity); DELETE /api/items/{id}.

Invalid input returns 400 with {"error": "..."}; unknown id 404. Data persists in the SQLite file across restarts. Concurrent requests must not corrupt data or lose updates (two simultaneous consumes of the last unit: exactly one succeeds).

UI (served at /): one responsive page that works at phone and desktop sizes. Include an "Expiring soon" section (next 7 days, expired items clearly marked), full list with search and an expiry filter, add-item form with inline validation messages, consume and delete actions, empty state and a visible error state when the API fails.

Keyboard accessible with visible focus; readable contrast; no horizontal scrolling at 375px. Clean, calm visual design. Use deliberate offline typography, spacing, contrast, clear language, purposeful accessible interaction, and brief motion that honors reduced-motion. Give the page an icon and serve every file it requests.

Import: `python import_items.py FILE.csv --db PATH` loads rows (name,quantity,unit,expires) into the same database, skipping invalid rows and printing one summary line "imported N, skipped M" (exit 0), or exit 2 with an error on an unreadable file.
The server, UI and importer work together from a fresh folder; a short README explains how to run them.
